name: Deep Slate-Blue
lede: Deep Slate-Blue is a dark, muted blue named for slate stone, recorded in Ridgway's 1912 atlas, carried into the ISCC-NBS system of 1955, and most over-represented in paintings from India.

sections.title: Named for the stone
sections.body:
Our data traces the name to slate, the grey-blue rock split into roofing tiles, a plant-and-landscape word in our tier system rather than a dye or pigment [1]. Ridgway's 1912 atlas plots it on plate XLIII at hue 49′′′, tone k, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the same area as block 186, "grayish blue" [1]. In LCH terms it measures lightness 38, chroma 12, hue 257 degrees: dark, lightly saturated, and a true blue rather than violet [1].

Its nearest distinct neighbor by computed color distance is [[dark-madder-blue|Dark Madder Blue]], 3.4 units away and read in our data as "purpler" [2]. [[black-coral|Black Coral]] sits almost as close, 3.4 units off as well, called "almost the same" [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, a close match covers enough of the canvas in 140, as photographed, more common than 64 percent of the named colors we track [3]. It peaks in paintings from the 1900s, at 2.7 times the rate expected from that century's share of the archive [3]. Niels Larsen Stevns is its most devoted painter here, with the color present in 5 of 22 of his works, seven times the baseline of the museums those works come from [3]. It is also most over-represented by country in paintings from India, at 2.3 times the expected rate, 13 of 721 paintings from there [3]. Its earliest archive match goes back to 1100, as photographed [3].
